newsitem.title: INDIA: India govt said owes IOC 45 bln rupees.
newsitem.headline: India govt said owes IOC 45 bln rupees.

text.p: The Indian government owes Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), the country's biggest refiner, 45 billion rupees through the state-run oil pool account, oil analysts said on Friday.
This represents over a 10 billion rupee increase over the arrears figure for the year ended March 31, 1996, they said.
IOC officials were not immediately available for comment.
IOC handles all of India's crude oil imports and most of its petroleum product imports.
The non-payment of dues to IOC however will not seriously hurt its profitability, an analyst at a leading brokerage said.
He said IOC was funding its projects largely through loans from the international market. "Interest payments and exchange fluctuations if any will be reimbursed by the government."
IOC's internal accruals were largely unaffected, he said.
The oil pool account owes smaller amounts to other state-run refining companies.
The government has begun disbursing arrears owed to Mangalore Refineries and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) after some delay, oil analysts said.
MRPL is a joint venture between state-run Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd and the private Aditya Birla Group of companies. All other refineries are state-owned.
The oil poll deficit is expected to rise to 80 to 90 billion rupees during 1996/97 from an earlier estimate of about 60 billion rupees, analysts said.
